transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um... well, I guess I came in because... I don't know, it's probably not a huge deal, but I just keep beating myself up a lot lately. 

I work in IT, and I just have this constant feeling that I'm not really senior material. Like I somehow just... fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. I feel a little silly even complaining about it, to be honest, because I know people deal with much worse. But it's just been weighing on me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm in the right place for this kind of thing.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge about things other than your work performance?

Um... no, I don't think so. It's really just the work stuff, mostly. Outside of that, I try to keep things pretty calm. I mean, I guess everyone gets a little stressed sometimes with everyday life, but I wouldn't say I'm constantly on edge or anything like that. 

I hope that's okay to say? I just... I don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart everywhere, because I'm usually pretty level-headed at home. It's just that feeling at the office. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
How long have you been feeling like you're not senior material at work?

Um... well, if I really think about it... it's been a while, I guess. I mean, not every single day, of course! I definitely don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all the time. 

But looking back, these sort of... low, guilty periods where I feel like I'm just faking it... they've been hanging around off and on for about eleven months now? Give or take? I hope that's not too vague of an answer. I usually just try to put on a brave face and push through it so I don't bother anyone, you know? Does that sound like a normal timeframe for this sort of thing?
Have you experienced any changes in your mood or interest in activities you normally enjoy outside of work?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want it to sound like I'm just sitting around doing absolutely nothing, because I do try to stay busy. But... well, usually on the weekends, I really look forward to firing up the grill, or maybe going fishing, or even just putting on a good record and relaxing. 

But lately... I don't know, I just sort of leave the grill covered up and the records sitting there. I just... I don't really care to do them as much right now. It's probably just a phase, right? I mean, everyone gets a little tired of their hobbies sometimes, don't they? I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or anything. I just haven't had the same energy for it. Is that what you meant?
Do you often feel worthless or inadequate outside of your concerns about work?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to be a good person, you know? I try to be a good neighbor, a good friend... I don't really sit around feeling worthless about my whole life. 

It's... it's really just the work thing. That's actually why I made the appointment to come in. I just... I keep beating myself up over it. I feel like I'm not really senior material, like I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. It's just this constant nagging feeling that they're going to figure out I'm in over my head. 

I hope it's okay that I'm focusing so much on the work aspect? I just don't want to make it seem like my whole life is falling apart, because it's not. It's just... I feel really guilty about letting them down at the office. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel guilty about things outside of your work performance?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to be a good husband, a good friend... I don't really walk around feeling guilty about my personal life. I hope that's okay to say? I don't want to sound like I think I'm perfect or anything, because I definitely make mistakes! 

But... yeah, it's really just the work thing. Like I mentioned before, that's the whole reason I'm here. I just... I keep beating myself up over it. I feel so guilty, like I'm not actually senior material and I somehow tricked everyone at the office into thinking I could handle all these responsibilities. I just feel bad that I'm letting them down. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Do you ever worry about things that might happen in the future when you're not thinking about work?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try not to be one of those people who just sits around worrying about every little thing that could go wrong. I like to think I'm pretty level-headed about the future, you know? 

It really does just come back to the job. That's the only thing that keeps me up at night, just... worrying that I'm not doing enough, or that I'm going to mess up a project and everyone will realize I shouldn't be in this position. But outside of that, no, I don't really have any big worries about the future. I hope it's not frustrating that I keep bringing it back to work? I just want to be as honest as I can so you get the right picture of what's going on. Is that helpful?
Do you feel like you're just pretending to be competent in other areas of your life, outside of work?

Oh, um... no, not at all. I feel like I'm pretty capable when it comes to my family, or just, you know, managing my day-to-day life. I definitely don't feel like I'm faking it there. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm bragging or anything! I just mean I feel okay about who I am outside of the office. 

I know I keep circling back to the exact same thing, and I'm really sorry if I'm sounding like a broken record... but that's honestly the whole reason I finally came in to see someone. I just constantly beat myself up over the job. I just have this heavy feeling that I'm not actually senior material, and I somehow fooled everyone there into thinking I could handle way more than I really can. But it really is just at work. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have these feelings about everything else? Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Do you feel like you're just pretending to be competent at work even when things are going well?

Yeah, actually... yes. Even when a project finishes and the client is happy, I... I don't really feel like I earned it. I just think, well, I got lucky this time, or my team carried me through it. 

I know I've said it a bunch already, and I'm really sorry to keep repeating myself, but that really is the whole reason I came in. I just... I can't stop beating myself up over it. I have this constant, awful feeling that I'm not really senior material, and that I've just... fooled everyone at the company into thinking I can handle way more than I actually can. 

I just feel like a fraud, I guess. I hope that makes sense? I know I shouldn't think that way when things are going fine, and I'm trying to be better about it, I really am. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you feel like you're just pretending to be competent in your current role even when you receive positive feedback or recognition?

Yeah, um... yes, even then. Like, if my manager says I did a good job on a system rollout, I just... I smile and say thank you, but inside I'm just thinking that they haven't looked closely enough at the code, or that the junior analysts did all the real heavy lifting. 

I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record here, and I'm so sorry for just saying the exact same thing over and over. But that's... that's really the core of it. I just came in because I keep beating myself up, constantly, over this idea that I'm not really senior material. I just feel like I've completely fooled everyone into thinking I can handle way more than I actually can. 

I hope it's not annoying that I keep coming back to that? I just... I want to make sure you understand how much it's weighing on me, but I also don't want to waste your time repeating myself. Am I doing okay explaining this?
Do you feel like you're just pretending to be competent in social situations outside of work?

Oh, no, um... socially, I feel pretty okay. I mean, I'm just a normal guy hanging out with friends or family. I don't feel like I'm putting on an act with them at all. I really hope I'm not making it sound like my whole life is a mess, because it's really not! I feel fine about who I am outside of the office.

But, um... yeah, I know I keep coming back to this, and I'm really, really sorry for repeating myself again. I just... I don't want to frustrate you. But it's just that work is the whole reason I'm here. I just can't stop beating myself up over it. I have this awful, sinking feeling that I'm just not senior material, and that I've somehow completely fooled everyone at the company into thinking I can handle all this stuff when I really can't. 

I hope it's okay that it's really just limited to my job? I know you're asking about other areas, and I want to be helpful... am I giving you the right kind of answers? I just want to make sure I'm doing this the way you need me to.
Do you experience significant anxiety when you are not thinking about work or your job performance?

Um, no, honestly I don't. If I can actually manage to get my mind off the office... I'm pretty relaxed. I don't really get anxious about normal, everyday things. I manage the rest of my life just fine, I promise. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just this total nervous wreck about everything, because I'm definitely not. It's really just... well, I know I've beaten it to death already, but it's really just the job. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, that it's mostly just contained to that one area of my life? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're looking for here. Is that the kind of detail you need?
Do you feel like you're not senior material even when you're working alone on a project?

Um, yeah... yes, even when it's just me and the computer. Honestly, sometimes that's when it hits the hardest. 

I... I know I keep coming back to this exact same point, and I feel terrible for just repeating myself again. I really hope you aren't sick of hearing it. But it's just... it's the whole reason I made this appointment in the first place. Even when I'm totally alone on a project, I just sit there beating myself up, completely convinced that I'm not actually senior material. I just constantly feel like I've fooled everyone into thinking I can handle all these responsibilities when I really can't. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's basically what I just told you a minute ago. I feel awful giving you the same answer again. Am I doing this right? I really want to be helpful and make sure I'm giving you the kind of information you need...
Do you still feel like you're not senior material after you've completed a project successfully and received recognition for it?

Um, yeah... even then. Even when a project goes well and people say good job, I just... I can't shake it. 

I feel so bad bringing this up again, I really do. I know I sound like a broken record, and I'm so sorry if I'm testing your patience. But that's just the core of it for me. It's why I'm here. Even with the praise, I just keep beating myself up, thinking I'm not really senior material and that I've just managed to fool everyone for another day into thinking I can handle more than I actually can. I always feel like they're just being nice, or that I just got lucky this time.

I hope it's okay that I'm being so repetitive. I just want to be totally honest with you so you can help me. Is it helpful that I'm clarifying that it happens even when things go well? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a complete picture.
Do you think you'll ever feel like you truly deserve your senior position, or will you always feel like you're just pretending to be competent?

Um, I don't know... I really hope so. I mean, I want to feel like I belong there. But right now... 

I know I'm probably frustrating you by saying this again, and I'm really sorry, but... it's just really hard to imagine feeling any different. Like I said, it's the whole reason I'm taking up your time today. I just can't stop beating myself up, thinking I'm not really senior material. I just constantly feel like I've fooled everyone into thinking I can handle all this, and eventually, they're going to figure it out. 

I really don't want to be a difficult patient, just saying the same negative things over and over. I want to get better, I really do. Do you think... I mean, from what I've been telling you, do you think it's possible for someone like me to actually get past this? I just want to make sure I'm not a hopeless case or anything...
Do you still feel like you're not senior material after receiving positive feedback from your colleagues or supervisor?

Um, yes... even when they say nice things. It's like... I hear the words, and I smile and say thank you, but inside... 

I know I'm saying the exact same thing again, and I'm so sorry. I really don't want to waste your time just spinning in circles. But honestly, it's the main reason I reached out for help. No matter what anyone says, I just keep beating myself up, completely convinced that I'm not really senior material. I just feel like I've somehow tricked them all into thinking I can handle these responsibilities, and the positive feedback just makes me feel guiltier, like I'm fooling them even more. 

I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you new information. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly. Is it okay that I'm feeling this way even when people are being supportive? I hope I'm not coming across as ungrateful to my team...
Do you feel like you're pretending to be something you're not in any areas of your life outside of work?

Um, outside of work? Not... not really, I don't think. I mean, I try to just be a good, normal guy at home and with my friends. I don't feel like I'm tricking them. It's really just... 

Well, I know I'm bringing it right back to the exact same thing again, and I sincerely apologize for being so repetitive. I really hope you're not getting frustrated with me. But it honestly all just comes back to my job. That's the whole reason I came in to see you in the first place. I just keep beating myself up over it, completely convinced I'm not senior material and that I've just... fooled everyone at the office into thinking I can handle more than I actually can. 

Is it okay that it's mostly just happening at work? I hope that makes sense, and I'm sorry if I didn't give you a better example for my personal life. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so you can understand where I'm coming from.
Do you think there was ever a time when you didn't feel like you were pretending to be senior material, even if it was just for a short while?

Um... let me think. Maybe right at the very beginning? Like, when they first gave me the title, I was just so busy trying to figure out the new systems and workflows that I guess I didn't really have time to second-guess myself. But... 

Oh gosh, I know I'm about to say the exact same thing again, and I am so, so sorry. I really don't want to sound like a broken record or make your job difficult. It's just... it always comes back to this overwhelming feeling. Like I said before, it's the entire reason I came in to see you today. Even if there was a brief moment where I felt okay, I just go right back to beating myself up, totally convinced that I'm not really senior material. The guilt is just really heavy... I just feel terrible, like I've completely fooled everyone into thinking I can handle way more than I actually can. 

I'm really trying to give you a better answer, I promise. Does that make sense at all? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you what you need to understand what's going on with me...
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't feel like you were pretending to be senior material?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, did I not answer that right just a second ago? I really apologize, I must have gotten off track or misunderstood. I'm trying my best to give you good answers, I promise. 

To try and answer you better... maybe right when I first got the promotion, like I mentioned, I didn't feel quite as bad because I was just focused on the new systems. But honestly... the whole reason I finally came in to see you is because I just keep beating myself up over this. I just have this constant, heavy feeling that I'm not really senior material, and that I've just... fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

Am I... am I understanding your question right this time? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need, and I feel terrible if I'm making you repeat yourself.
Do you feel inadequate or like you're pretending to be something you're not in any aspects of your life outside of work?

Oh, gosh... I am so sorry. You asked me about outside of work earlier, didn't you? I must be doing a terrible job explaining myself if you have to ask it again. I feel awful making you go in circles like this. I'm really trying my best to give you the right answers, I promise. 

To be completely honest, outside of work... no, I don't really feel inadequate. I just try to be a normal, dependable guy for my friends and family. It really is just the job that's the problem. Like I said, that's the whole reason I came in to see you. I just keep beating myself up, constantly worrying that I'm not really senior material. I just feel like I've fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can. 

Does that help clarify things a bit better? I really hope I'm giving you what you need this time, but please let me know if I'm still not making sense...
